sentences.text: Callovosaurus is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur known primarily from a nearly complete left thigh bone found in Middle Jurassic rocks in England.
The type specimen's thigh bone is 28 cm long, suggesting the animal was approximately 2.5 meters in length.
The fossil was collected from the Peterborough Member of the Oxford Clay Formation near Peterborough in Cambridgeshire, England.
The species was first described by Richard Lydekker in 1889 under the name Camptosaurus leedsi.
Peter Galton established the new genus Callovosaurus for the species in 1980.
Callovosaurus was a herbivore, feeding on plant material like other iguanodontians.
It is probable that Callovosaurus traveled in herds to protect itself from predators, a behavior inferred from better-known ornithopods like Iguanodon.
The validity of Callovosaurus has been debated, with some researchers considering it a dubious genus or a basal dryosaurid.
A 2025 study found Callovosaurus to be more basal than previously thought and placed it outside the families Dryosauridae and Dryomorpha.
Callovosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 162 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
The time range for Callovosaurus is estimated to be between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
Callovosaurus lived alongside diverse reptiles including ichthyosaurs, plesiosaurs, crocodyliforms, pterosaurs, sauropods, stegosaurids, and the armored dinosaur Sarcolestes.
